paragraphs.source_en: After weathering crisis after crisis, the road gradually grew wider. They had now entered the sphere of activity of Kameya Einin, the Kyoto cloth merchant who had gone on ahead, and Chaya Shirōjirō. At last they could greedily snatch half an hour's sleep, then change their straw sandals and prepare to cross the steep mountains of Marubashira. Seeing that Ieyasu now enjoyed the wholehearted protection of warriors from Iga and Kōga, Kameya and Chaya were reassured and took their leave.

paragraphs.source_en: Now that they were armed, all that remained was to battle the physical agony of going without sleep or rest. They still frequently encountered lawless mountain bandits and robbers on the road, but no one could stand against them now. The time in his life when Ieyasu learned the most was this day and night of travel from Marubashira through Kawai, Tsuge, and Kabuto, along the banks of the Suzuka River, to the Sea of Ise.

paragraphs.source_en: Ieyasu remembered the past, when he had still been Imagawa Yoshimoto's hostage in Sunpu. While expounding the teachings of Mencius, the Zen master Sessai had often quoted a certain line so that Ieyasu might inherit the spirit of cherishing the people: “Heaven sees with the eyes of my people; Heaven hears with the ears of my people.”

paragraphs.source_en: Perhaps this was a man sent to him by the Zen master Sessai! As he walked, Ieyasu kept looking at Magoshirō, subjecting himself to a severe self-examination. Unless one listened to the voice of the people, one would never discover the truth...

paragraphs.source_en: From Shiroko Beach to Tokoname on the Chita Peninsula, there were no vessels except the small firewood boats that took the shortest route. Yet now not even one of those small boats was available. This district had originally lain within Oda Nobutaka's sphere of influence. But Nobutaka, intending to cross the sea to Shikoku, had already led his forces to Kishiwada, and nearly all the large vessels in his territory had therefore been requisitioned and gathered near the port of Sakai.
